body:
This is interesting, it means that the extended lifetime countdown doesn't "start" until the owner set is empty, and the owner set doesn't become empty until the shared worker's event loop stops processing its last task ([here, right](https://whatpr.org/html/11600/56a15bf...b97f311/workers.html#worker-processing-model:concept-WorkerGlobalScope-owner-set-2)?).

This, I think, puts the lifetime countdown starting time in the shared worker's hands to some extent, so I think we might be susceptible to what @asutherland was trying to avoid in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10997#issuecomment-2877998342:

> a lifetime deadline/grant based on when its last owning window goes away (and not based on when the SharedWorker is told about it to avoid attempts to extend lifetime by clogging up the task queue that might delay such a notification)

I could be totally wrong on this though, since I haven't read the entire PR yet? Thoughs?

body:
You're right to be cautious about this. However, I think we're OK:

- If a document is destroyed, then it gets taken out of the owner set immediately. So if all owners are destroyed, it doesn't matter if any tasks are ongoing in the worker, the timer will start.
- Similarly, if a document moves to bfcache (not fully active), it will hit step 4.1.2, again regardless of any tasks in the ongoing worker.

Let me know if there's something missing though.

body: This is a bug that I'll fix in the next 24h (it's currently late where I am). If a shared worker has an owner set: [bf-cached-doc, fully-active-doc] and we iterate over this list in order, we will evaluate bf-cached-doc first, and return true/false depending on how long it's been non-fully-active. But because the shared worker has at least one fully active doc, it is thus independently "actively needed" and should never be "in extended lifetime".

body: This is not the recommended range for implementers. The normative requirement for implementers is outlined elsewhere to be no longer than the amount of time a service worker with no clients is allowed to stay alive. This is just an example for developers, basically. I guess we could supply a _lower bound_ so that it can't be significantly less than the time here, but since implementers agree on the current spec, I'd ask you to file a follow-up bug to discuss with people, if there's an appetite for changing this.
